lines.trans: Tariq! Where did this shining blue-and-brass tin box come from?!
Bought it at the hardware shop on Thursday afternoon, just in case.
Wait—you were already planning a brand-new time capsule two days ago, Tariq?!
That hollow pocket under the third courtyard stone is already lined with good brick.
Seems a shame to leave good brick engineering empty for the next thirty years, right?
Exactly my thought: pure practical maintenance, zero sentiment involved.
Zero sentiment, says the man who already cut a fresh square of yellow beeswax linen!
Watch your jokes, Nour, or you will not get to write the lid label.
Oh, please let me write the label! What year and message should we put on top?
Write: Opened with friends in May—please open again thirty summers down the road.
Who gets to choose what treasures go inside our new courtyard capsule tonight?
Call Salma, Suad, and the brothers in here—everyone adds one honest piece of this week.

meanings.note: Takes a long -uu-/-oo- stem with possessive endings in Jordanian (أخوي my brother, أخوك your brother); dual أخوين.

examples.trans: My older brother lives in Amman.
The brothers sat together in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Literally 'I beg/hope of you'. Uses -ak/-ik/-kum endings depending on whom you address (أرجوكي to a woman, أرجوكم to a group).

examples.trans: Please let me write the new label!
Please wait a moment by the door.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: زرقا, plural: زرق).

examples.trans: The blue suitcase is in the luggage closet.
I have two blue teacups.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أسابيع.

examples.trans: Next week I have time off.
We stayed at the guesthouse all week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: صفرا, plural: صفر).

examples.trans: A yellow taxi stopped outside the gate.
The yellow lemon cake is ready.

أصلا.gloss: anyway; in the first place; actually

meanings.en: anyway; in the first place; actually
meanings.note: Everyday conversational adverb meaning 'in the first place / anyway / to begin with'.

examples.trans: Does the attic even have a comfortable bed?
The wire needed adjusting anyway.

meanings.note: Form IV hollow verb (بضيف / ضفت). Used for adding an item to a box, list, or recipe.

examples.text: كل واحد بيضيف تذكار صغير للعلبة.
examples.trans: Everyone adds one small keepsake to the tin.
We added a little honey and orange zest.

meanings.note: Exclamation of mild surprise or realization ('oh!').

examples.trans: Oh! My glasses are on my head!
Oh, look at the beauty of this ceiling!

meanings.note: In questions أي means 'which?' (أي علبة؟ 'which tin?'); in conditionals/negatives it means 'any' (أي شي 'anything').

examples.trans: Which tub of butter did you bring?

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

meanings.note: Jordan, Syria, Lebanon and Palestine use the old Syriac-derived month names: كانون التاني January ... أيار May ... أيلول September.

examples.trans: My birthday is in May.
In May the weather gets nice in Amman.

meanings.note: Core Jordanian everyday verb for 'to come' (إجا / بيجي).

examples.trans: You came ten minutes early.
I will come on Friday at noon.

meanings.note: Means 'except / unless' (إلا إذا 'unless') and 'minutes to the hour' (اطنعش إلا خمسة 'five to twelve').

examples.trans: It is five minutes to twelve!

examples.text: ما حدا بيقيس الساحة إلا مهندس!
examples.trans: Nobody measures a courtyard except an engineer!

meanings.note: Often placed directly after a noun in Jordanian to mean 'spare' (مفتاح احتياط a spare key).

examples.trans: I have a spare key in the drawer.
We bought a spare valve for winter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بختار, بيختار).

examples.trans: I chose this quarter for a family reason.
They chose a table under the tree.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بستنى, بيستنى).

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بشتري, بيشتري).

examples.trans: Tell me exactly what to buy.
Buy both brass valves together.

meanings.note: Name of the fifth day of the traditional Arabic week ('Thursday', related to خمسة 'five').

examples.text: السوق الشعبي بيفتح يوم الخميس بعد الظهر.
examples.trans: The neighbourhood market opens on Thursday afternoon.

examples.text: رح نستلم الطاولات يوم الخميس الجاي.
examples.trans: We will receive the tables next Thursday.

meanings.note: Invariant spoken Jordanian relative pronoun ('who, which, that') for any gender or number.

examples.trans: That is what I want.
The inn that keeps a stranger's bag safe.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنتبه, بينتبه).

examples.text: انتبه على راسك من الخشب الواطي.
examples.trans: Watch your head on the low beam.
Be careful of the corner chair.

meanings.note: The n-pattern of فتح: the thing opens by itself, nobody is named (الباب انفتح 'the door came open').

examples.trans: The window blew open by itself in the wind.
The old lock does not open easily.

meanings.note: Signature Jordanian/Palestinian pronunciation (with z) of بالضبط ('exactly!').

examples.trans: Exactly! You have become one of us.
Tell me exactly what to buy.

meanings.note: Colloquial Levantine adverbial phrase meaning 'at all' in negatives (ما شفته بالمرة) or 'altogether / completely'.

examples.trans: I did not rush the playing at all today.

examples.text: الموضوع هاد عملي بدون عاطفة بالمرة.
examples.trans: This matter is practical with zero sentiment at all.

meanings.note: Preposition 'without'; followed by ما + verb it means 'without -ing' (بدون ما ياخد 'without taking').

examples.text: شاي أحمر بدون سكر لو سمحتي.
examples.trans: Black tea without sugar, please.
I entered the booking without my glasses!

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

meanings.note: Means 'after' (بعد المطر) and with a future span 'in' (بعد أربعين دقيقة 'in forty minutes').

examples.trans: He arrives in forty minutes.
How lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تالتة, plural: تالتين).

examples.trans: The attic room is on the third floor.
He used to sit on the third step.

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('under, beneath') and standalone ('downstairs').

examples.trans: Let us bring it downstairs into the light.
The wide desk is under the window.

meanings.note: Masculine noun for a memento or keepsake (plural: تذكارات). From the same root as تذكّر ('remember').

examples.text: كل واحد حط تذكار صغير بالعلبة.
examples.trans: Everyone put one small keepsake in the tin.

examples.text: هاي الخريطة أحلى تذكار من أستاذنا.
examples.trans: This map is the loveliest keepsake from our teacher.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بترك, بيترك).

examples.text: مين ترك هاد المغلف جنب الجرس؟
examples.trans: Who left this envelope by the bell?
Thank you for not leaving me in the rain.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Quick thinking solved the problem.
That is smart, logical thinking.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'thirty'.

examples.trans: They have given us thirty days in the letter.
The bill is thirty-eight dinars.

meanings.note: Active participle of إجا ('to come'): means 'on the way / arriving' (جايين 'they are coming') and after a time noun 'next' (الأسبوع الجاي 'next week').

examples.trans: The guests are coming down the stairs now.
We will see you next week!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: جديدة, plural: جداد).

examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.
I installed a new lightbulb last week.

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('inside the bag') and standalone ('inside').

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
The water is flowing inside!

meanings.note: Masculine noun for a pocket or hollow recess (جيب الطوب 'the brick pocket'). Plural: جيوب.

examples.text: هداك الجيب تحت الحجرة مبطن بطوب.
examples.trans: That pocket under the stone is lined with brick.
He put the small key in the coat pocket.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: حجار.

examples.trans: Old stone holds warmth.
She stepped onto the stone step outside.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحط, بيحط).

examples.trans: Where should I put the spoons and napkins?
I put the suitcase beside the table.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to speak, talk, tell' (بحكي / حكى).

examples.trans: Salma chats with all the neighbours.
Tell me everything I need to know.

meanings.note: Feminine noun (plural خسائر) widely used in Jordanian speech as an exclamation: خسارة! ('what a shame!').

examples.text: خسارة نترك شغل طوب ممتاز فاضي!
examples.trans: It is a shame to leave good brick work empty!

examples.text: يا خسارة، خلصت الكيكة قبل ما نوصل.
examples.trans: What a shame, the cake ran out before we arrived.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخطط, بيخطط).

examples.trans: Did you plan this entire meeting?
We planned to open the café in spring.

meanings.note: Very frequent Jordanian verb: خليني ('let me'), خلينا ('let us'), خليك ('stay!'), خلي ('keep/leave').

examples.trans: Let us open the door together.
Hot bread makes people pleasant!

دخل.gloss: to enter; come in; go in

meanings.en: to enter; come in; go in
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بدخل, بيدخل).

examples.text: تفضل ادخل من المطر يا أستاذ.
examples.trans: Please come in out of the rain, sir.

examples.text: الزوجين دخلوا غرفة ستة قبل ساعة.
examples.trans: The couple checked into room six an hour ago.

راح.gloss: to go; be gone (راحت علينا we missed our chance)

meanings.en: to go; be gone (راحت علينا we missed our chance)
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بروح, بيروح).

examples.trans: We missed our chance — he hung up!

examples.text: كل التعب راح مع أول فنجان قهوة.
examples.trans: All the tiredness vanished with the first cup of coffee.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: رسايل.

examples.trans: An official letter arrived at noon.
We read the letter line by line.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine/Jordanian word for 'man / guy' (plural: زلم). Warm and conversational.

examples.text: الزلمة اللي قص القماش جاهز من زمان!
examples.trans: The man who cut the cloth was ready long ago!
Tariq is a kind man with a big heart.

meanings.note: Masculine noun for time as an epoch or span (كبسولة زمن 'time capsule'). Plural: أزمان.

examples.text: عملنا كبسولة زمن جديدة لتلاتين صيف.
examples.trans: We made a new time capsule for thirty summers.

examples.text: من زمن بعيد والناس بتشرب شاي هون.
examples.trans: From long ago people have drunk tea here.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسمح, بيسمح).

examples.trans: Take the guesthouse number, please.
Allow me to pour the orange juice.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: سنين.

examples.trans: The building is eighty years old.
I have not seen him for three years.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أشغال.

examples.text: حبيت الشغل هون من أول يوم.
examples.trans: I loved the work here from day one.
Let us finish our work before noon.

meanings.note: Collective masculine noun for wax (شمع عسل 'beeswax') or candles (singulative شمعة).

examples.text: لفينا العلبة بقماش شمع العسل الأصفر.
examples.trans: We wrapped the tin in yellow beeswax cloth.
We put small candles beside the lanterns.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: صحاب.

examples.trans: Who is the owner of the blue suitcase?
We became friends from the first day.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: صادقة, plural: صادقين).

examples.trans: A short, sincere sentence from the heart.
Be honest with your brother.

meanings.note: Everyday word confirming something is right ('right! / true!').

examples.text: صح! في صفحة تانية ورا الرسالة.
examples.trans: Right! There is a second page behind the letter.
What you say is completely true.

meanings.note: Masculine noun for tinplate or sheet metal (علبة صفيح 'tin box').

examples.text: اشترى علبة صفيح زرقا جديدة لكبسولة الزمن.
examples.trans: He bought a new blue tin box for the time capsule.
Tin keeps the papers dry in the sand.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.trans: Regular maintenance protects the building.
We called the maintenance technician in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Evenings in Amman are pleasant in summer.
Our rent is paid until next summer.

meanings.note: Collective noun for bricks or building blocks; حيط طوب is a brick wall.

examples.trans: The house is built of brick and stone.
They brought new bricks for the wall.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: عواطف.

examples.trans: Good maintenance has nothing sentimental about it!
He spoke with his brother with genuine warmth.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: عدد.

examples.trans: The screwdriver and wrench are in the toolbox.
He brought the tools to fix the boiler.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Here is mint tea with honey.
Mountain honey tastes wonderful.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: عصور.

examples.trans: We arrived at the guesthouse Monday afternoon.
Late-afternoon tea in the courtyard is a daily ritual.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: علب.

examples.trans: The gold tin is on the top shelf.
I saved this old wooden box.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from عمل ('work/action'); describes someone focused on practical details.

examples.trans: Mazen is more practical than that.
This is a practical and quick solution.

meanings.note: A lid of a pot, box or piano; also a blanket for the bed.

examples.trans: Put the lid on the pot.
In winter I sleep under a heavy blanket.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: فاضية, plural: فاضيين).

examples.trans: Is room six vacant tonight?
The street outside the gate is completely empty.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفتح, بيفتح).

examples.trans: The corner shop opens at seven.
Oh, the door finally opened!

في.gloss: there is; there are; is there?

meanings.en: there is; there are; is there?
meanings.note: Spoken Levantine existential word ('there is / there are'); negated as ما في ('there is no / there are no').

examples.trans: There is a small paper tag on the handle.
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Means 'before' (قبل الفطور) and with a time span 'ago' (قبل ساعة 'an hour ago', قبل شوي 'just now').

examples.text: علمت بيانو هون قبل خمسة وعشرين سنة.
examples.trans: I taught piano here twenty-five years ago.
Drink your coffee before the rush.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قريبة, plural: قراب).

examples.text: علمت بيانو ببيت قريب من هون.
examples.trans: I taught piano in a house near here.
We booked a table at a nearby restaurant.

قص.gloss: to cut; snip; trim (with scissors or shears)

meanings.en: to cut; snip; trim (with scissors or shears)
meanings.note: Geminate verb for cutting stems, paper, or tape cleanly.

examples.text: لا تقص عرق الياسمين الأخضر، ارفعه لفوق.
examples.trans: Don't cut the green jasmine stem—lift it upward.
I cut a strip of black tape for the wire.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: قطع.

examples.trans: Please have a piece of warm bread.

examples.text: خبزت كيكة مع قطع زوايا زيادة.
examples.trans: She baked a cake with extra corner pieces.

meanings.note: Any fabric; سلك قماش is old cloth-covered electrical wire.

examples.trans: She bought blue fabric for the curtains.
This fabric is very soft.

meanings.note: Arabic uses no 'is/are' in the simple present, while كان supplies the past ('was/were') and يكون / بيكون supplies future or modal 'be'.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day will not be boring!

meanings.note: Loanword used for medicine capsules and also in the phrase كبسولة زمن ('time capsule').

examples.trans: We opened the time capsule today.
The capsule was placed under the soil.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بكتب, بيكتب).

examples.text: رح يكتب تقييم حلو عن النزل.
examples.trans: He will write a lovely review of the guesthouse.
I wrote my name and number on the card.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite singular noun كل means 'every' (كل يوم 'every day'); before a definite noun it means 'all / the whole' (كل الأسبوع 'all week').

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: Masculine noun (pl. كنوز); literally buried treasure, and used playfully for cherished keepsakes.

examples.trans: I like treasures that shine.
This notebook is a treasure for the family.

meanings.en: to shine; to gleam; to sparkle
meanings.note: Sound Form I verb (بلمع / لمعت) from root ل-م-ع, used for polished metal or bright ink.

examples.trans: The drawings still shine on the paper.
The brass lock gleamed in the sun.

meanings.note: Introduces polite requests (لو سمحت 'if you please') and hypothetical conditions ('if').

examples.trans: Take the guesthouse number, please.
Even if he is a little late, wait for him.

meanings.note: Definite الليلة means 'tonight', while indefinite ليلة means 'one night / night of'.

examples.trans: I am going to sleep well tonight.
We booked the room for three nights.

meanings.note: Negates verbs and في (ما بعرف 'I don't know', ما في 'there isn't'), and links conjunctions like قبل ما ('before') and بعد ما ('after').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Form II passive participle from root ب-ط-ن ('lining/inside'), describing boxes, coats, or envelopes.

examples.trans: The box is lined with blue fabric.
The jacket is lined with warm wool.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian noun for any retail shop or spot (pl. محلات).

examples.trans: Below is the signature of the antique shop.
There's a pastry shop next to the house.

meanings.note: Masculine verbal noun (masdar) from مزح ('to joke'); used in expressions like بلا مزح ('no kidding').

examples.trans: The jokes are all ordinary teasing.
I'm speaking seriously, not joking.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Dual ملصقين ('the two labels'), plural ملصقات ('labels / stickers').

examples.text: نور كتبت ملصقات واضحة وكبيرة لكل المرتبانات.
examples.trans: Nour wrote big, clear labels for all the jars.

examples.text: تأكد إن الملصقين ناشفين قبل ما تمسك القزاز.
examples.trans: Make sure both labels are dry before you pick up the glass.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ممتازة, plural: ممتازين).

examples.trans: The reading light beside the desk is excellent.
The shower water was hot and excellent!

meanings.note: Everyday preposition meaning 'from', 'of', or 'than' after comparatives.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian question word for 'who?' (لمين 'whose? / for whom?').

examples.trans: Who left this envelope here?
Whose is this brown leather notebook?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنادي, بينادي).

examples.trans: Do we call each other by first name here?
Salma called everyone to breakfast.

meanings.note: In Jordanian Arabic, نحاس covers both yellow brass and red copper, often placed directly after a noun (مفاتيح نحاس brass keys).

examples.trans: We polished the brass keys in the morning.
The brass pot is old and engraved.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian demonstrative ('this / that'); feminine هادي (haadi), plural هدول (hadool). Before ال- it also contracts to هال-.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine singular demonstrative (هاي مدرسة الروابي، هاي أول مرة).

examples.trans: This is my friend Dina.
This idea is excellent.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian distal demonstrative ('that over there / that past...'); feminine هديك (hadiik), plural هدولاك.

examples.text: بتذكر هداك الربيع لما فتحنا النزل؟
examples.trans: Do you remember that spring when we opened the inn?

examples.text: حط الصندوق على هداك الرف العالي.
examples.trans: Put the box on that high shelf.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian/Levantine word for 'here' (لهون 'to here', من هون 'from here').

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
Stay right here a minute.

meanings.note: Used both as the numeral 'one' and after a noun for emphasis ('a single, one and the same').

examples.trans: Not a single scratch on the cup!
The gate rang with one strong ring.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine pronunciation of وجه (wajh, 'face'), heard constantly in Amman speech.

examples.trans: His face was beaming in the photo.
Wash your face with cold water.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian question word for 'where?'.

examples.trans: Where is the computer, Tariq?
Where should I put the small spoons?

meanings.note: Placed directly before a name or title when addressing someone in Arabic (يا نور 'Nour!', يا أستاذ 'sir!') and in exclamations (يا سلام! 'wonderful!').

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أيام.

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!
